text:
maria: quick sync — i'm worried hard-rejects during bursts will break customer SLOs. can we explore backpressure that degrades gracefully?
aj: +1. idea: non-blocking admission that returns a short 'defer' response with estimated wait, so caller can retry or route to cheaper model variant.
sahil: how do we prevent cost blowouts if many tenants are rerouted to expensive fallbacks? need per-tenant cost smoothing / budget.
maria: propose: a token-bank per tenant (capacity + refill) that drives admission decisions. when empty, we return a soft-defer or offer fallback instead of immediate hard 503.
cheng: fallback tiers: quantized smaller model, lower concurrency region, or a queued slow-path. prefer cheaper-model fallback first.
liz: product note — fallbacks must be visible in the Console and opt-in per-route. customers should see cost/latency tradeoffs.
aj: technical sketch: local fast-path consumes ephemeral credits from an in-process cache, long-term source is distributed counter (redis/raft). local hits avoid round-trip on the common case.
sahil: agree on local cache, but replenish logic needs jittered backoff to avoid thundering-herd during heavy drains. also expose metrics: bank_depth, spill_count, fallback_rate.
maria: config example (POC):
```
admission:
  mode: backpressure
  token_bank:
    capacity: 1200
    refill_per_min: 300
    local_cache: 50 # ephemeral local buffer per node
  fallbacks:
    - type: cheaper_model
      names: [gptx-small-q4, gptx-compact-q8]
    - type: region_fallback
      regions: [us-east-1, eu-west-1]
  guardrails:
    max_cost_multiplier: 2.0 # block fallback if it would exceed this
    only_for_requests: ["stateless", "short"]
```
aj: admission API change idea: return structured hint in response headers: `X-RW-Admission: defer;eta=120;route=compact-q8` so clients can decide.
cheng: caveat: KV-cache warmup — switching to a smaller model invalidates cache usefulness and may spike token counts. heuristic: only allow model fallback for requests with prompt_len < 512 and no expected multi-turn state.
sahil: ops: add circuit-breaker that escalates to hard-reject when overall infra is saturated for X minutes to protect cluster stability.
maria: rollout plan: feature-flag, internal tenants first, surface metrics + alert if fallback cost delta > threshold.
liz: i'll draft a short product doc on opt-in and Console UX showing fallback impact per-route.
aj: i'll prototype the distributed token bank (redis-based) + local cache and wireup the `X-RW-Admission` header. posting PR when ready.
sahil: i'll add SLO tests that simulate bursty tenants to verify graceful degradation and cost smoothing.
maria: one more constraint — ensure tenants can opt-out entirely to get hard-fails (some customers want strict capacity limits). add `admission.behavior: hard` per-tenant.
deploy-bot: feature-flag `admission.backpressure` toggled in staging :white_check_mark:
liz: sounds good. can we capture these semantics in a short RFC section? i'll start the draft and tag reviewers.
aj: will attach POC config and basic benchmarks next week.
maria: thanks all — next check-in Friday at 11am.
